meta.title: Carnegie Mellon's AP CSP in Python

locator_titles.1: Unit 1: Intro to CMU Graphics (Drawing Basics, More About Drawing, Create Task Design)
locator_titles.4: Unit 4: Complex Conditionals, More Events, and Libraries
locator_titles.5: Unit 5: Create Performance Task (supplemental, used with/in place of Code.org's own CPT unit)
locator_titles.supplemental: Optional: Supplemental Materials (Nested Loops, 2D Lists, Project Practice)

meta.caveat: Covers only CMU's own programming units -- by the teacher's own instruction, nothing from Code.org's units is included here (see codeorg-apcsp.json). apcsp and castandards entries are this carrier's own read of CMU's pacing guide and the co-branded syllabus's Big-Idea tags -- direct, lesson-level evidence. csta2017 entries are NOT independently sourced: they're mechanically derived from this carrier's own castandards codes via _standards/crosswalk-castandards-csta2017.json, so treat them as exactly as confident as the castandards claim they ride on, never as a separate confirmation. csta2026 and ca-ict-anchor entries are this carrier's own topic-level inference, kept deliberately sparse -- included only where a unit's content is a clean, specific match, not forced onto every unit.

1.1.note: Unit 1's Create Task Design section (Intro & Creativity and Planning) and Unit 5's Create Performance Task both center on the pair/individual creative-project format CMU calls a Creative Task.

1.2.note: Create Task Design (Unit 1) and the Create PT itself (Unit 5) both require students to state a program's purpose before building it.

1.3.note: Unit 1's 'Intro & Creativity and Planning' step and Unit 5's design guide + example graded projects are CMU's own program-design-and-development materials for this product.

3.1.note: Unit 2's dedicated Variables lesson (Mouse Events week 2), after general shape Properties.

3.4.note: Unit 4's Strings lesson, paired with Types and Input the same week.

3.6.note: Unit 2's if-else Conditionals and if-elif-else lessons.

3.7.note: Unit 4's Complex Conditionals lessons: Compound conditionals and Nested conditionals, named as such.

3.8.note: Unit 3's Traversing Groups / Traversing a list with len and range. The optional Supplemental unit adds Nested For Loops; the optional Test Prep unit's 'Robot and While Loops' lesson is this product's only evidence of a real `while` loop -- indefinite iteration, not just the `for`-style traversal the core 4-unit sequence teaches.

3.9.note: From the (optional) AP Test Prep unit -- not required for the AP exam, and not part of the 4-unit core pacing guide's 56 class days. Test Prep's own 'Algorithms' and 'Simulations' review lessons.

3.10.note: Unit 3's Lists, Traversing a list, and List methods lessons. The optional Supplemental unit extends this to 2D lists.

3.12.note: Unit 2's Function Basics and Multiple Parameters; Unit 4's 'Functions that Return Values' lesson.

3.13.note: Unit 2's Function Basics lesson pairs a 'Debugging and Test Cases' sub-lesson with function development from the start.

3.14.note: Unit 4's own Libraries lesson (Functions that Return Values, Random Numbers) and Using Media (Images).

3.15.note: Unit 4's Random Numbers lesson, under the Libraries heading (Python's random library).

3.16.note: From the (optional) AP Test Prep unit -- not required for the AP exam, and not part of the 4-unit core pacing guide's 56 class days. Test Prep's own 'Simulations' review lesson.

1.4.note: Unit 2's Function Basics week pairs a named 'Debugging and Test Cases' sub-lesson with the function-writing lesson -- the only unit in this product's pacing guide with debugging named as its own sub-lesson.

9-12.AP.12.note: Unit 3's loop/traversal work chooses and adapts algorithms over groups and lists; Test Prep's Algorithms review lesson makes the same skill explicit.

9-12.AP.13.note: Lists and Groups (Unit 3) are core, assessed content, not an optional add-on -- same argument cmu_cs1.json makes for its own units 10-11.

9-12.AP.14.note: Conditionals (Unit 2), nested/compound conditionals (Unit 4), and Test Prep's explicit while-vs-for loop comparison ('Robot and While Loops') are all control-structure choices this standard names.

9-12.AP.16.note: Function Basics, introduced in Unit 2, is decomposition into subproblems -- same argument cmu_cs1.json makes for its own unit 3.

9-12.AP.17.note: Unit 4's Libraries lesson (calling pre-written library code, including media) is modular design via library calls.

9-12.AP.18.note: The Create PT's design guide and example graded projects are explicitly audience-facing (a real AP exam submission an outside reader scores), a stronger claim than cmu_cs1.json can make for its own Creative Task, which only has a feedback step if the teacher builds one in.

9-12.AP.19.note: Not taught in this product's pacing guide -- software license limitations aren't named in either source PDF, matching cmu_cs1.json's own explicit gap for its unit-19 equivalent.

9-12.AP.20.note: The Create PT is a build-reflect-revise cycle by design (practice Create Tasks, then the graded submission); the syllabus PDF tags this unit's collaborative option with CTP1/CTP3/CTP4/CTP6.

9-12.AP.21.note: The syllabus PDF explicitly offers a collaborative Creative Task grouping option for the unit that maps onto this product's Unit 5.

9-12.AP.22.note: The Create PT's own written-response prompts about the finished program are documentation of design decisions -- the CPT cannot be submitted without them.

HS-PRO-PD-12.note: This carrier's own inference, not an official document: Unit 2's Function Basics lesson splits a program into functions, the construct this standard names.

HS-PRO-VD-16.note: This carrier's own inference: Unit 3 has students choose between Groups and Lists to hold a program's data, the choice this standard names.

HS-PRO-TR-19.note: This carrier's own inference: Unit 2's named 'Debugging and Test Cases' sub-lesson, and the Create PT's own practice-then-submit structure.

HS-PRO-TR-20.note: This carrier's own inference: the Create PT's design guide and example graded projects imply a revise-from-feedback step, though (as with 9-12.AP.18 above) CMU's own materials don't require one.

HS-ALG-PS-02.note: This carrier's own inference: wrapping repeated steps in a loop, over Groups/Lists (Unit 3) and again over 2D lists (optional Supplemental unit).

HS-ALG-PS-04.note: This carrier's own inference: Unit 4's Random Numbers lesson is the clearest instance of a program that doesn't give the same result from the same input.

C4.9.note: This carrier's own inference, quoting the standard's own language: 'a shared toolkit of constructs -- branches and loops, reusable functions' is exactly Units 2-4's Conditionals, Loops, and Functions content.

C4.7.note: This carrier's own inference: Groups and Lists (Unit 3) are the data-structure content this standard names.

C5.6.note: This carrier's own inference: Unit 2's named Debugging and Test Cases sub-lesson treats debugging as part of building the program, not a separate step -- this standard's own framing.
